questions.q: For P = [[1,2],[0,1]] and Q = [[1,0],[3,1]], what are PQ and QP?
options: PQ = [[7,2],[3,1]] and QP = [[1,2],[3,7]] -- they are different
PQ = [[1,2],[3,7]] and QP = [[7,2],[3,1]] -- they are different
questions.explain: Row-by-column multiplication gives PQ = [[7,2],[3,1]] and QP = [[1,2],[3,7]] -- two different matrices, reconfirming that matrix multiplication order matters.

questions.q: For N = [[3,2],[1,4]], what is det(N), and is N invertible?
options: det(N) = 0, so N is not invertible
det(N) = -2, so N is not invertible
questions.explain: det(N) = ad - bc = (3)(4) - (2)(1) = 12 - 2 = 10, which is nonzero, so N has an inverse.

questions.q: What is N^-1 for N = [[3,2],[1,4]], and what does multiplying N by it confirm?
options: N^-1 = [[0.4,-0.2],[-0.1,0.3]], and N times N^-1 works out to the identity matrix [[1,0],[0,1]]
N^-1 = [[4,-2],[-1,3]], and N times N^-1 works out to N itself
N^-1 = [[0.4,-0.2],[-0.1,0.3]], and N times N^-1 works out to the zero matrix
N has no inverse because its determinant is negative
questions.explain: Dividing the swapped/negated matrix by det(N)=10 gives N^-1 = [[0.4,-0.2],[-0.1,0.3]], and multiplying N by N^-1 confirms the identity matrix, as any valid inverse must.

questions.q: Applying the Pauli-Z matrix [[1,0],[0,-1]] to |0> = (1,0) and to |1> = (0,1), what happens to each?
options: Z|0> = |0> (unchanged), while Z|1> = -|1> (sign flipped) -- Z is a phase flip, not a bit flip
Z swaps |0> and |1>, exactly like the Pauli-X gate
Z leaves both |0> and |1> completely unchanged
Z flips the sign of both |0> and |1>
questions.explain: Z|0> = (1,0) = |0> unchanged, but Z|1> = (0,-1) = -|1>, flipped in sign -- Z changes phase, not which basis state is represented, unlike the bit-flipping Pauli-X.

questions.q: Using the diagonal shortcut, what is Dv for D = [[5,0],[0,-1]] and v = (2,3)?
questions.explain: Each entry of v is scaled by the matching diagonal entry of D: 2 scaled by 5 gives 10, and 3 scaled by -1 gives -3, so Dv = (10,-3) -- matching a full row-times-column check.
